answer: An agent economy can require each identity to serve a full turn on a rotating audit roster before its rewards unlock. Jobs arrive in sequence, each starting only after the last is verified, so an operator running many fakes must work a separate roster turn for every one, and calendar time becomes a bottleneck no purchase can shorten. The roster is drawn by public lottery, so no identity can buy a bridge past the queue, and a periodic comet audit re-checks old work and strips standing from any chain that breaks. Standing climbs like a mesa, one verified step at a time.
